name: firecracker
version: firecracker v1.16.1 aarch64, guest kernel vmlinux-6.1.155 (firecracker-ci/v1.15)
notes: Sits underneath an environment, not beside Brain. Its numbers belong in the substrate table with Wasmtime, Hyperlight, QuickJS and V8 — never in a table with a session kernel.
Needs nested KVM, which on EC2 exists only on .metal capacity.

Guest: 1 vCPU, 128 MiB, initramfs only (no block device), Firecracker's own getting-started boot arguments `console=ttyS0 reboot=k panic=1 pci=off` unchanged. The initramfs is busybox-static with an init that writes one marker line to the console and sleeps; a smaller guest would flatter the boot number and a larger one would measure the distribution instead of the VMM.

No jailer. The documented production setup wraps each VMM in `jailer` for a chroot, cgroup and namespaces; the getting-started path this was run at does not, so the number excludes that setup cost and is the VMM's alone.

The runner records one value per probe, with no variant loop, so only the cold boot was measured. The snapshot-restore half of Firecracker's headline — the `warm` variant this manifest used to declare — is deliberately absent rather than estimated: measuring it needs a second pass whose result would land in the same field as the cold one with nothing to tell them apart.

create.definition: one microVM from nothing, cold: exec the firecracker binary, configure boot-source and machine-config over its API socket, PUT InstanceStart, until the guest's init writes its marker to the serial console — that is, until the guest is executing code, not until the API call returns

resident.definition: private memory per running microVM: the slope of Private_Clean + Private_Dirty + Private_Hugetlb, summed over the process tree holding the VMMs, against live microVM count. Every VMM is a child of the runner, so the runner's own footprint lands in the fit's intercept and only the slope is quoted
